description:
`Bedrock.Cluster` declares:

    @type capability :: :coordination | :log | :materializer | :resolution   (lib/bedrock/cluster.ex:23)

but `ClusterSupervisor.module_for_capability/1` only handles three of those:

    defp module_for_capability(:coordination), do: Coordinator   # cluster_supervisor.ex:253
    defp module_for_capability(:materializer), do: Foreman
    defp module_for_capability(:log), do: Foreman
    defp module_for_capability(capability), do: raise("Unknown capability: #{inspect(capability)}")

So configuring a node with `capabilities: [:resolution]` -- a value the public typespec says is legal -- raises during `Supervisor.init/1` and the node fails to start.

Either resolution is a real per-node capability and the dispatch is missing, or it is not and the typespec is lying. Dialyzer will not catch this: the raise clause is reachable for any atom, so the spec and the implementation never get compared.

Found while building the peer-cluster test harness (bedrock-80f), where the typespec was the natural source of truth for which capability combinations to test.
title: [BUG] :resolution capability is in the typespec but ClusterSupervisor raises on it
